restated: For all integers q >= r >= 0, f(q,r) <= q + r + 1. Consequently, for each fixed r the quantity f(q,r) - q is at most r + 1 for every q >= r.
ledger_statement: For all q >= r >= 0, f(q,r) <= q + r + 1. Proof: induction over the three branches of the recurrence. In the mex branch the set {f(a,r):a<q} u {f(q,b):b<r} has at most q+r elements, so among the q+r+1 positive integers 1..q+r+1 one is missing and the mex is at most q+r+1; the r>q branch gives f(q,q) <= 2q+1 <= q+r+1; the stale branch gives f(q-1,r) <= q+r. Corollary: max_q (f(q,r)-q) <= r+1, which discharges (Z1) of byrnes_audit.md with C=1.

verdicts.gap_description: The stated claim is proved correctly: in branch (C), |S| <= q + r is valid as a union bound (no distinctness needed), so mex(S) <= q + r + 1, and branches (A),(B) follow. The deficiency is not a gap in the proof of the value bound but a gap relative to the project target: the corollary bounds the values of f(q,r)-q, not the preperiod N(r), and the submission explicitly concedes that no bound on N(r) is supplied. Novelty of this elementary pigeonhole lemma is not established.

verdicts.gap_description: No gap found. The induction is well-founded under lexicographic order on (q,r): branch (A) reads (q,q) with q<r (same first coordinate, smaller second), branch (B) reads (q-1,r) (smaller first coordinate), and branch (C) reads (a,r) with a<q and (q,b) with b<r. All three branches of the recurrence are handled, and the mex argument is valid: S has at most q+r elements, so among the q+r+1 integers 1..q+r+1 at least one is absent, forcing mex(S) <= q+r+1.
